<reason>Side A won by making the clash decidable: a pension credit is a vested claim on other workers, not delayed care pay, so messy verification and “see the carer” can support cash/respite without minting contribution years. Side B’s verification trap and existing-credits comparison were sharp, but the fiscal “cheap if care happens anyway” line was internally weak, compounding was never shown to be a mere difference of degree, and two clipped turns were an execution cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s R2/closing split: time-limited care benefits can live with a rough gate because the error dies; a credited year compounds and bills strangers—defusing B’s verification-hypocrisy trap without abandoning support for carers.</best_rebuttal>
